text:
incident-bot: on-call handoff: mike_ops -> tara_s starting now. quick summary below. :wave:

mike_ops: handing off early due to timezone swap. short TL;DR: saw a burst of 429s on /v1/embeddings between 20:07-20:15 UTC. root cause is autoscaler oscillation on the embedding worker group (scale up/down thrash). we applied temporary mitigation by shifting traffic to emb-fallback and raising max replicas. no customer data loss, but increased p95 and a handful of customer retries. logging and traces are in the runbook link.

tara_s: thanks — quick question, which route is emb-fallback? link pls.

mike_ops: emb-fallback is model: redwood/embedding-small-v2, route /v1/embeddings?policy=fallback. runbook: https://redwood.internal/runbooks/embedding-autoscale. also here's the autoscaler cache tweak we pushed: 
```bash
kubectl -n inference set env deployment/emb-autoscaler MAX_REPLICAS=12 STABILIZATION_WINDOW=60
```
we also bumped the HPA target CPU from 60 -> 75 for the short term.

sophia_reliability: observed spike in queue length in prometheus: 
`sum(rate(emb_queue_length[1m]))` jumped x5. dashboards updated; alerting suppressed for 10m while we stabilize.

henry_oncall: any customer-facing impact? did support page customers get pages?

mike_ops: a few retries surfaced in support (incidents ticket #2241). impact: increased latency and ~0.03% 5xx rate from retries, mostly recovered after reroute. we proactively opened a single issue to notify high-traffic customers; no SLA breach expected.

aisha_se: noted for customer comms. recommended wording: "We experienced elevated latency on embeddings for ~8 minutes due to autoscaler instability and rerouted traffic to a fallback model while we stabilized capacity. We do not expect data loss; normal service resumed after mitigation."

tara_s: ok taking primary. current status: embedded fallback still receives ~12% traffic. autoscaler set to MAX_REPLICAS=12. monitoring: watch p95, queue_length, hpa_desired_replicas. I'll keep alerting on. primary/secondary: tara_s (primary), sophia_reliability (secondary) for next 4h window.

henry_oncall: coverage gap? do we need extra coverage for APAC region? the fallback is in us-west only.

tara_s: good call — APAC saw minor elevation but under SLO. plan: enable cross-region failover if we see >0.5% error rate sustained for 10m. opening a ticket to enable pre-warm in ap-southeast: infra ticket #AP-78.

incident-bot: runbook pointer: https://redwood.internal/runbooks/embedding-autoscale (playbook steps, rollback commands, escalation matrix).

mike_ops: next steps I left in the playbook: 1) keep max_replicas=12 for 30m, 2) monitor queue_length and p95, 3) if p95 > 700ms for 10m then failover routing to emb-hot-2, 4) follow up with model team to tune batching. also note we disabled prefix-caching for a small subset (temp) — see commit `prefetch:disable-202603` in infra repo.

sophia_reliability: adding a small watchlist: `emb_req_5xx`, `emb_p95`, `emb_queue_length`, `hpa_desired` — slack alerts to #eng-oncall and pager policy to primary only for now.

tara_s: I'll run the post-mortem checklist if we get a repeat. immediate action items for me: 1) confirm AP-78 ticket creation, 2) sanity check the HPA metric mapping, 3) schedule a short sync with model infra tomorrow. leaving detailed notes in the incident doc.

mike_ops: leaving the thread — anything you want me to keep an eye on before I log off?

tara_s: if you can follow up on whether prefetch disable caused any regression in throughput that'd be great. otherwise i'm good. thanks for the handoff. :thumbsup:

henry_oncall: assigned roles confirmed. primary: tara_s, secondary: sophia_reliability. escalation: henry_oncall if both unavailable. coverage notes: APAC watchlist created.

incident-bot: handoff complete. reminders: attach post-incident notes to ticket #2241, and set incident severity if we end up with followups.
